title: Is a US–Iran deal getting closer? Plus a deadly tanker strike off Qatar
summary: Bloomberg reports the US and Iran edging toward a deal with Iran's nuclear programme back on the table, a seafarer killed on the tanker Velos Sapphire north of Qatar and another blast off Khasab, a reported strike on the Afipsky refinery, the latest front-line numbers, and a Houthi missile aimed at Medina.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Friday, November sixth. And for once, the lead story is about a possible step toward ending a war, not escalating one.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. Bloomberg reports that the United States and Iran are edging closer to a deal. And the key detail is that Iran's nuclear programme is back on the table.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's significant, because until now Tehran had kept nuclear issues out of these talks. According to a diplomat who spoke to Bloomberg, Iran is now weighing proposals from Qatar, the main mediator, on its atomic activities.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: But there's a catch. An Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran did send a nuclear proposal through Qatar. But discussing it, he said, depends on Washington first meeting Iran's seven demands.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And those include lifting sanctions, releasing frozen Iranian assets, and compensation for the war.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the US side, President Trump spoke with Qatar's emir about the talks. And he said he had no immediate plans for new strikes on Iran, which pushed oil prices lower.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Though, to be fair, he's also been saying the world will know very soon whether he chooses a deal or more strikes. So the door is open both ways.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the human cost at sea keeps rising while all this plays out. We mentioned a tanker hit north of Qatar yesterday. Now we know more.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The ship is the Velos Sapphire, a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker managed by Velos Tankers in Athens. It was sailing empty to Bahrain. The operator says an unidentified projectile likely hit the stern on the port side.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And one crew member was killed. He'd first been reported missing, then was found fatally injured. The crew put out the fire, and there's no reported pollution.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: To put that in context, the International Maritime Organization says it has now confirmed one hundred and twenty-nine incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region, with twenty-five seafarers killed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And there was another one. Late on Thursday, an outbound tanker reported an explosion on its port side, near the waterline, about sixteen nautical miles east of Khasab, in Oman. That's right in the strait.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Luckily, that ship kept going under its own power, and all the crew are safe. UKMTO hasn't said who was responsible.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Okay, let's turn to Ukraine. It's been a slightly quieter couple of days, at least compared to earlier this week.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Ukraine's long-range drone campaign continues, though. Kyiv Post reports a drone attack on the Afipsky refinery in Russia's Krasnodar region overnight. Russia says it shot down a hundred and forty-two drones. Officials haven't confirmed any damage at the refinery.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And that would be one more refinery on a long list this fortnight. Novokuybyshevsk, Ufa, Kstovo, Yaroslavl, the Samara oil hub, and then Ryazan yesterday.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line, Ukraine's General Staff reported a hundred and eighty-eight clashes on Thursday. The heaviest fighting was again around Pokrovsk, with sixteen Russian attacks, and Kostiantynivka, with eleven.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the air war over the front is intense. Seventy-nine Russian airstrikes, dropping two hundred and thirty-five guided bombs, in a single day.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On diplomacy, yesterday was the White House meeting on the Oleshky ceasefire, and technical talks in Brussels on reconstruction. Next week the big one is the trilateral round in the United Arab Emirates.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now, the other fronts. Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed a missile the Houthis fired toward Medina, Islam's second holiest city. The Houthis hadn't claimed any attack.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the second time in a week the coalition has reported a Houthi weapon aimed at a holy city. Last week it was a drone near Mecca, which the Houthis denied.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Gaza, rescue services say Israeli strikes and gunfire killed five people on Thursday, including a woman and a twelve-year-old boy.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in southern Lebanon, Al Jazeera and Lebanon's state news agency reported Israeli strikes on Kfar Tebnit, in Nabatieh district, and al-Mansouri, in Tyre district.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the ships, no change today. The Theodore Roosevelt was last reported in the South China Sea, heading west toward the Middle East. The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush are in the Arabian Sea.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. Whether this nuclear opening becomes real negotiations, or stalls on Iran's seven demands. Whether attacks on shipping in the Gulf keep spreading. And the Ukraine talks in the UAE next week.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Plus the next fleet tracker on Monday, which should tell us where the Roosevelt has got to.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you next time.
